hints: Sort points by x, breaking ties by y.
Build lower and upper chains, removing turns that bend inward.
Keep collinear boundary points: remove only strict clockwise turns.
analogy: Stretch a rubber band around the points, retaining every point lying on its boundary.
example: For (0,0),(1,0),(2,0),(2,1),(0,1), all five points lie on the hull boundary.
algorithm: Sort points lexicographically. Build lower and upper chains in opposite orders; while the last two chain points and the new point make a strict clockwise turn, remove the last point. Append the new point. Concatenate chains, omitting duplicated endpoints. Use wide cross products.
correctness: Each chain removes exactly inward bends and retains collinear edge points. The resulting two outer chains bound all points and contain every input point on the boundary.
complexity: For n points, O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
